model: negative-binomial GLM; median-of-ratios size factors; gene-wise dispersions shrunk to a fitted trend
multiple_testing: Benjamini-Hochberg with independent filtering on mean count (DESeq2 results() default)
assumptions: raw integer counts, one library per experimental unit; NB mean-variance; fixed effects
reference: Love, Huber & Anders 2014, Genome Biology 15:550; vignette 'Analyzing RNA-seq data with DESeq2'

model: negative-binomial GLM with quasi-likelihood dispersion; TMM normalisation; empirical-Bayes QL dispersions
assumptions: raw integer counts, one library per experimental unit; fixed effects
reference: Chen, Lun & Smyth 2016, F1000Research 5:1438; edgeR User's Guide

calls: edgeR::normLibSizes + limma::voom + lmFit + eBayes; duplicateCorrelation for one random grouping term
model: precision-weighted linear model on log2-CPM (voom weights from the mean-variance trend)
random_terms: one random grouping term, as a within-group correlation (duplicateCorrelation, two voom passes)
assumptions: raw counts; log2-CPM approximately normal given voom weights
reference: Law, Chen, Shi & Smyth 2014, Genome Biology 15:R29; limma User's Guide

model: precision-weighted linear mixed model per feature (lme4), random terms as written in analysis.model
test_statistic: moderated t with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom
assumptions: raw counts; repeated or nested units modelled by the design's random terms

calls: limma::lmFit + eBayes; duplicateCorrelation for one random grouping term
model: linear model per feature with empirical-Bayes moderated variances
assumptions: values approximately normal on the input scale; fixed effects plus at most one grouping term
reference: Smyth 2004, Stat Appl Genet Mol Biol 3:3; Ritchie et al 2015, Nucleic Acids Res 43:e47

calls: DSS::DMLfit.multiFactor + DMLtest.multiFactor(coef), on methylated and total reads pooled per window
model: beta-binomial regression with arcsine link, general design
assumptions: methylated and total read counts per region and unit; overdispersion shared by the beta-binomial prior
reference: Park & Wu 2016, Bioinformatics 32:1446; DSS vignette, section 'general experimental design'

calls: edgeR glmQLFit on IP and input libraries together, design = library type x the design's fixed terms; glmQLFTest on the IP x treatment interaction
model: negative-binomial GLM; the enrichment change is the library-type x treatment interaction, so expression changes (seen in input too) cancel
assumptions: IP and input counts per window for the same units; IP and input share the expression change
reference: the IP x condition interaction GLM used by exomePeak2 and RADAR; edgeR User's Guide (interaction designs)

model: per-feature linear model with the design's fixed terms; empirical-Bayes variance moderation re-implemented from limma's squeezeVar
random_terms: dropped (fixed terms only, with a warning)
assumptions: as limma; fallback only, used when no gold-standard engine is installed

model: Gaussian linear model with the design's fixed terms
test_statistic: t per coefficient; F per term (anova)
assumptions: independent units, normal residuals, equal variance

model: Gaussian linear mixed model, REML, random terms as written in analysis.model
test_statistic: t with Satterthwaite df; F per term
assumptions: normal random effects and residuals
reference: Bates et al 2015, J Stat Softw 67(1); Kuznetsova et al 2017, J Stat Softw 82(13)

model: logistic regression
assumptions: independent 0/1 outcomes

model: logistic mixed model (Laplace)
assumptions: normal random effects on the logit scale
reference: Bates et al 2015, J Stat Softw 67(1)

model: negative-binomial GLM, log link
assumptions: independent counts, NB variance

model: negative-binomial mixed model, log link
assumptions: NB counts, normal random effects on the log scale
reference: Bates et al 2015, J Stat Softw 67(1)

model: Cox proportional hazards on time + event
assumptions: proportional hazards; independent censoring

model: GLMM by Laplace approximation (TMB); same formula as analysis.model
assumptions: as the family; normal random effects

model: mixed-model GWAS: kinship (A.mat) random effect, PCs as fixed covariates, variances fitted once (P3D)
test_statistic: -log10 p of the marker F test
random_terms: the line effect is the kinship random effect
estimate_scale: marker effect not reported (estimates from the native scan)
assumptions: line means (BLUEs) as phenotypes; additive markers

model: compressed mixed linear model GWAS (kinship + PCs)
random_terms: the line effect is the kinship random effect
assumptions: line means as phenotypes; additive markers

model: EMMAX: kinship random effect, PCs fixed, REML variances once, GLS per marker
random_terms: the line effect is the kinship random effect
assumptions: as rrBLUP P3D; fallback when rrBLUP is not installed

model: cumulative logit (proportional odds) model
assumptions: proportional odds

model: Cox proportional hazards with normal random effects (mixed-effects Cox model)
assumptions: proportional hazards; independent censoring given the random effects; normal random effects
reference: Therneau TM, coxme (R package); Ripatti & Palmgren 2000, Biometrics 56:1016

model: Cox proportional hazards with a gamma frailty for one grouping factor
random_terms: one random intercept, as a gamma frailty
assumptions: proportional hazards; gamma-distributed shared frailty
reference: Therneau, Grambsch & Pankratz 2003, J Comput Graph Stat 12:156

model: proportional-odds cumulative logit model
assumptions: proportional odds; independent units
